question.problem: In the right triangle $△JKL,$ $∠J$ is a right angle, $JL=8$ and $KL=12.$ Find $\operatorname{tan}⁡K.$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246155/assets/cc33327cc6d071cb6ec9ac0c10d58e57bc35f8d81b326731120cf04c18f58ec1.png)

Recall the definition of tangent: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡K=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{JL}{JK}=\frac{8}{JK}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing side $JK.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}JK & =\sqrt{K{L}^{2}-J{L}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{12}^{2}-{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144-64} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡K & =\frac{8}{4\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
